models: Esquire (the 'Born to Run' guitar, a hybrid Tele
guitar.evidence: Springsteen's battered Telecaster/Esquire hybrid is one of the most iconic guitars in rock, featured on countless album covers.

tone.target: dry warm edge-of-breakup Springsteen rock crunch
tone.profile: dry warm edge-of-breakup Springsteen rock crunch
tone.summary: A warm, slightly overdriven signal chain using a US Deluxe or Silver Twin model into a 2x12 cabinet, enhanced by a light boost and subtle room reverb to capture the classic Springsteen rock sound.
corrections: drop delay as a main color
keep it drier and more direct

rig.name: Bruce Springsteen - The River - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and pick attack transients.
Provide the necessary 'edge-of-breakup' crunch and tighten the pick attack without sounding overly distorted.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate a light, clean boost pedal (like an early Tube Screamer setting) for mid-range focus.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use a very subtle gain stage if the Boost is insufficient. Keeping it 'None' allows the amp to handle all breakup.
blocks.gap: The primary crunch comes from the preamp and amp model, so no dedicated distortion unit is needed.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Fender-style clean-crunch tone, providing warmth and mid-forward punch.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative if the US Deluxe is too bright.

blocks.purpose: Match the Fender-style sound and complement the US Deluxe amp model.
Slightly scoop the bass and boost the mids to achieve the required 'mid-forward crunch' and warmth.
No wah needed; the focus is on direct, punchy chords.
Avoid delay wash as requested; keep the sound direct.
Provide a subtle 'hint of room reverb' to add depth without washing out the dry punch.

alternatives.reason: If a slightly brighter, more defined room sound is desired.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better cabinet realism and warmth.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Fender-Ampeg crunch with more realistic tube character.
